text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Friday:
-- Credit Suisse First Boston (CSFB), part of the Credit Suisse Group, is cutting 700 jobs in Switzerland as it transfers its operational centre to New York.

-- Zurich city health councillor Wolfgang Nigg denounces national referendum drive for a hard-line anti-narcotics policy called Youth Without Drugs. Nigg said a total ban on withdrawal aid methadone, included in the proposal, would leave around 15,000 drug addicts in Switzerland the choice between illegal consumption, prison and abstinence-oriented longtime-therapy. The vote will be in September.

--About 50,000 people checked an Internet site listing names of foreigners who opened now-dormant accounts in Swiss banks before May 1945. The number was the total in the first 36 hours after Swiss banks published the list on Wednesday in an effort to find the heirs of Holocaust victims with Swisss accounts. Over 1,000 people called one claims contact office in Basel in the first three hours on Wednesday for information kits. Four other offices in New York, Budapest, Sydney and Tel Aviv received many calls as well.

--Denner Holding, which runs a Swiss chain of discount supermarkets and is also politically active, is hiring 400 people with a budget of 150,000 Swiss francs to gather signatures for two referendum drives it supports. OLne referendum would bring lower retail prices for pharmaceuticals and the other wants faster handling of referendum petitions that can now take years to get to the ballot box. Several politicians critisised the move as damaging to direct democracy. Denner officials said the paid signature drive was more effective and cheaper than advertising in newspapers.

--The Federal Competition Commission has made a preliminary decision to take action against four domestic Swiss health insurers that cover about 70 percent of insured customers in Switzerland. The commission decided to investigate suspicions that Helsana, Visana, CSS and Konkordia had a confidential agreement to work together for seek higher premiums.
